name: CWO World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The CWO's own top belt, tracked week by week across the fed's self-published Rankings ledger from the moment the 1997 corpus opens (Master of Darkness Damion, carried over from 1996) through Lord Hile Troy's title-changing swerve at the CWO Celebration on 14 December 1997, when the operator's own on-screen persona turned on the man he had spent the match seconding.

name: CWO North American Championship
epitaph: The fed's secondary singles belt, changing hands ten times across 1997 and ending the year on Fergus "Whirling Scottish Devil" McTavish.

name: CWO Television Championship
epitaph: The CWO's television title, vacated once for a ten-man battle royal at ST. VALENTINE'S DAY MASSACRE II and closing 1997 on Wildfire.

name: CWO Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Contested at 240 lbs. and under; Moses held it three times across the year, a fact the fed's own 9 November 1997 HOTLINE corroborates directly ("the Light Heavyweight Championship, which he held three times during the past year").

name: CWO World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's top tag title, opening 1997 with the Creatures of the Night (dated on-air to a September 1996 win) and closing it with the Deadly Sins.

name: CWO North American Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's secondary tag title, closing 1997 on Riders on the Storm.

name: CWO World 6-Man Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A three-on-three tag title that drops out of the fed's own Rankings ledger after the period ending 27 July 1997 and is not carried into the fed's 1998 continuity -- an honest gap in the record, not a claimed retirement of the belt.

name: CWO FEVER Championship
epitaph: A singles title tied to the FEVER broadcast, held by Brad Wheatley after the 2006 MADNESS tournament and then by Surge, who defended it against Flame in April 2006.

name: CWO International Championship
epitaph: A singles title held by Rt Savage as of April 2006, defended outside a non-title Tables, Ladders and Chairs match he lost to Marc Meredyth.

name: CWO Amazons Championship
epitaph: The CWO's own women's title, changing hands from Amy Savage to Ms. Rose in a three-way match on EXTREME, 9 April 2006.

name: CWO Amazons Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A new women's tag title, first contested and won by Shadows of Heaven (Angel and Lita Dumas) in a 5-team battle royal at the CWO's own tenth-anniversary pay-per-view, FOREVER, 30 April 2006.

name: CWO EXTREME Championship
epitaph: A new singles title, introduced vacant and won by Prince David Tita in an 11-man pinfall/submission battle royal at FOREVER, 30 April 2006.

name: CWO International Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A tag title defended alongside the CWO World Tag Team Championship, first attested held by the Falconi Brothers and won from them by South Street Riot in a no-tags hardcore match, 8 May 2006.

name: CWO Trios Championship
epitaph: A three-man title reinstated at the federation's own INFERNO pay-per-view, 25 June 2006, first won by Nightrain, Ryan Welfare and Jimmy Page.

name: CWO Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Born from a unification match that absorbed the CWO Light Heavyweight Championship in September 1999.

name: CWO Women's Championship
epitaph: Created vacant for the 2001 EXTREME MEASURES relaunch and won in a three-way match on the promotion's own 9 May 2001 broadcast, the first title made for the wing's own newly opened women's division.

name: EWA World Tag Team Championship
notes: The invading EWA's own tag team belts, presented in the ring and not recognised by the CWO.
epitaph: The invading EWA's own tag team championship: its leader presented the belts from a metal briefcase to the Pit Bosses on the FEVER of 1 February 2002, the CWO announcers said it would not be recognised, and the Pit Bosses were billed as its champions through 10 February, saying they meant to unify it with the CWO tag titles. One reign on record.
